answer: Cross-correlation lag detection: each agent action emits a signed timestamp; the system clusters behavior across an "opal" graph of interaction fingerprints. Sybils coordinating in lockstep produce abnormally tight temporal correlation and near-identical "tundra" action sequences. A "jetty" threshold flags clusters whose mutual information exceeds organic baselines. Attacker cost: must simulate diverse, decorrelated behavior across many identities, raising compute and coordination overhead per fake agent until marginal cost exceeds expected yield.
